title: Deuteronomy
author: Moses is traditionally understood as the author of Deuteronomy, with the closing record of his death added after his lifetime.
date: Traditionally connected with the final days of Moses before Israel entered the promised land.
audience: The new generation of Israel standing on the edge of the promised land, called to remember the Lord, love Him, and obey His covenant.
historicalSetting: Deuteronomy records Moses' final addresses to Israel on the plains of Moab. He reviews the Lord's works, restates the law, calls Israel to covenant faithfulness, and prepares them for life in the land.
themes: The promise of a prophet like Moses
keyVerse: Deuteronomy 6:4-5 — "Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one. You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might."
christFocus: Deuteronomy points to Christ as the promised Prophet like Moses, the faithful Son who perfectly loved and obeyed the Father, and the One who bore the curse to redeem His people. It calls hearts to love the Lord fully, a life made possible through Christ and the work of the Holy Spirit.
outline: Review of Israel's wilderness journey — Deuteronomy 1-4
The covenant and the call to love the Lord — Deuteronomy 5-11
Laws for worship, holiness, and covenant life — Deuteronomy 12-26
Blessings, curses, and covenant renewal — Deuteronomy 27-30
Moses' final words, song, blessing, and death — Deuteronomy 31-34
